assumptions.summary: Braking is neglected because braking-force data are unavailable and crash avoidance is assumed rare in individual time trials.
Lateral movement is neglected because a 1 m/s lateral velocity is less than one percent of professional forward speed above 10 m/s.
All bicycles are standardized to the same size as a fairness and modeling convention.
Cyclist posture is averaged as constant because elite riders maintain a stable posture over extended periods.
The drivetrain is treated as 100 percent efficient and gear selection is excluded from the control formulation.
Baseline air density is constant and unaffected by elevation in the dynamics model, then a separate temperature sensitivity modifies density.
Maximum speed is constant throughout simulations, including sharp-turn cases, and final position is fixed while velocity and energy remain uncertain.

contributions.summary: Use spherical geometry and route coordinates to construct local distance and slope inputs.
Replace a two-parameter CP curve with a three-parameter finite-Pmax model for rider profiles.
Couple remaining anaerobic energy, adjusted recovery, and energy-dependent Pmax.
Integrate fatigue/recovery with nonlinear force dynamics and effective wheel-inertia mass.
Use PMP and complementarity to derive a small candidate control set.
Use Bellman backward recursion and value iteration to produce a deterministic policy.
Apply the policy to Tokyo, UCI, and San Felice routes with profile-specific time costs.
Re-optimize for wind geometry and compare route-shape sensitivity.
Separate deviation-probability sensitivity from location/terrain sensitivity.
Formulate six-rider drafting and lead-time optimization based on fourth-finisher time.
Translate the model into a three-principle race guidance memo and preparation checklist.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Training Peaks supplies 5 s, 1 minute, 5 minute, and functional-threshold powers for gender/type profiles.
STRAVA-Tokyo2020 supplies latitude, longitude, and altitude for the 2021 Olympic time-trial course.
STRAVA-BelgiumUCI supplies route coordinates and altitude for the 2021 UCI World Championship men's course.
Adjacent route points are approximately 600-1000 m apart and are converted through spherical angle, straight-line distance, and elevation slope.
Posture constants use Cd=0.88, A=3.9 ft^2, rho=1.29 kg/m^3, and CR=0.015; wheel radius and inertia standardize effective mass.
Temperature sensitivity uses a 20 C baseline and 0.5-degree positive/negative steps on the Tokyo women's specialist case.
Deviation probability and location experiments use repeated measurements on the Tokyo women's course, with location sections every 2 km and p=0.1 for the location study.
The team extension labels six riders A-F and uses front-lead durations as schedule inputs, but no raw schedule or solver is supplied.

independent_extensions.summary: Fit the three-parameter CP model with uncertainty, profile-level residual diagnostics, and held-out horizons.
Use an explicit nonnegative fatigue/recovery state with dimensional energy accounting and calibrated Padj dynamics.
Replace constant-rho and fixed-vmax assumptions with coupled altitude, temperature, braking, turn-radius, and posture states.
Run DP grid-refinement, positivity, v=0 handling, runtime, and policy-stability tests with reproducible code and seeds.
Repeat wind and deviation experiments with published randomization, replicates, uncertainty intervals, and route arrays.
Solve six-rider lead schedules with workload, transition, drop, fourth-finisher, and drag-calibration constraints.

results_trace.summary: three-course comparison: Tokyo -> UCI -> own design -> four cyclist profiles. Boundary: Keep course lengths and gender-specific routes visible.
finish-time disclosure: rider profile -> course -> minimized seconds. Boundary: Report exact units and avoid comparing unlike route lengths without qualification.
start-power recommendation: all rider types -> high initial power -> backstretch CP. Boundary: Attach the recommendation to the model's control set and course.
uphill/downhill recommendation: uphill -> maintain power; downhill -> low power -> rest. Boundary: Keep the recommendation conditional on the simplified force model.
route-closure result: San Felice route -> descent -> start/finish same place -> Figure 13. Boundary: A designed route claim should be checked against coordinates if reused.
weather-motivation opening: gusty wind/high temperature -> performance impact -> sensitivity need. Boundary: Separate weather motivation from measured sensitivity.
wind-angle definition: wind angle theta -> cycling direction phi -> relative drag. Boundary: Use one angular convention throughout the wind equation and plots.
lateral-effect reduction: lateral assumption -> directional drag -> one-dimensional wind force. Boundary: The result inherits the lateral-motion assumption.
course-shape interpretation: route geometry -> wind-direction regularity -> sensitivity pattern. Boundary: Interpret regularity as a geometry effect in the tested routes.
density-cascade setup: temperature/altitude -> pressure -> density -> power profile. Boundary: Carry the temperature chain through all intermediate variables.
temperature-grid design: 20 C baseline -> plus/minus 0.5 C steps -> Figure 16. Boundary: Report baseline, step, rider, and course for the curve.
temperature-result interpretation: nonextreme range -> lower temperature -> lower time -> equipment/hydration advice. Boundary: Keep the advice within modeled temperature and density assumptions.
probability perturbation: ideal distribution -> sampling points -> shift probability p -> repeated minimum times. Boundary: State the perturbation distribution, replicates, and seed if available.
probability monotonicity: higher p -> higher time cost -> pacing stability. Boundary: Monotonic trend from a scatter plot is not a global theorem.
location perturbation: Tokyo women course -> 2 km sections -> fixed p=0.1 -> repeated times. Boundary: Keep location and probability effects separate.
terrain-specific sensitivity: uphill sections -> larger impact; downhill sections -> smaller impact. Boundary: The terrain conclusion inherits the force and deviation assumptions.
checkpoint uncertainty: critical point -> ideal arrival -> plus/minus deviation. Boundary: Attach units, section, probability, and repetitions to each interval.
terrain-guidance close: uphill rhythm -> downhill rest/high speed -> practical pacing. Boundary: Translate the table into action without claiming safety validation.
team-resistance opening: front rider -> windward area -> largest drag -> lead workload. Boundary: Separate leader burden from follower benefit.
drag equation: density -> drag-reduction coefficient -> Cd/A/v -> D. Boundary: Define Cdr and Cd before using team strategy language.
lead-rotation principle: fixed order -> 10-30 second lead -> position change -> dropped weak rider. Boundary: Treat this as cited strategy context, not measured optimal timing.
team-objective declaration: six riders -> fourth finisher -> minimum time objective. Boundary: Keep the fourth-finisher rule in the objective.
team-time parameterization: rider labels A-F -> front durations -> order function L(s) -> objective J. Boundary: Define decision variables and schedule constraints before claiming optimization.

weaknesses.summary: The two-parameter CP critique motivates the three-parameter model, but four profile points do not establish physiological superiority or robust extrapolation.
Wprime, w, wrec, Padj, a, and b are not given a complete common unit and state-normalization convention.
The baseline dynamics treats rho as constant while the temperature section later changes rho; the two implementations are not reconciled.
The term u/(m v) is singular at v=0, yet the initial velocity and transition handling are not disclosed.
The effective-mass formula, drag term, and force notation mix bicycle/cyclist mass and acceleration units without a full dimensional closure.
vmax is held constant even for sharp turns, while braking is omitted, so turn feasibility is not physically represented.
PMP provides necessary conditions and four cases, but sufficiency, transversality, and boundary conditions are not demonstrated.
The Bellman/value-iteration pseudocode does not state state-grid resolution, action grid, transition probabilities, theta, runtime, or convergence diagnostics.
Wind drag Eq.36 names FW as drag force but divides by mass; units and directional sign conventions require reconciliation.
The pressure relation and temperature-altitude relation use unclear units and are not connected to an independent atmospheric calibration.
Temperature advice is inferred from a local 0.5 C sweep around 20 C and should not be generalized to extreme weather.
Deviation plots omit random seed, number of replicates, perturbation distribution, and uncertainty interpretation for the intervals.
The team model defines front times and a fourth-rider objective but does not solve a schedule, enforce workload transitions, or calibrate Cdr.
Memo recommendations about hydration, equipment, psychological confidence, and following other players extend beyond the fitted model and safety evidence.
There is no appendix or complete executable code/data package, so the DP and route simulations cannot be end-to-end reproduced from the PDF alone.
